dialogues.speaker: Yolotli
dialogues.text: Hello, hello... Did Mr. Toltec ask you to come find me?

dialogues.speaker: Yolotli
dialogues.text: Did I seem a bit nervous to you? Yeah, sorry about that.

dialogues.speaker: Yolotli
dialogues.text: Thing is, a message from Mr. Toltec often means a new commission to investigate the Ley Lines. But I'm afraid I'm not ready to go out there again quite yet.

dialogues.speaker: Yolotli
dialogues.text: There are many mystical arts that need learning, and materials that must be prepared in advance...

dialogues.speaker: Yolotli
dialogues.text: My Ley Line perception is mediocre, so I need Saurian help for that — and Iktomisaurs aren't the type to just go out for walkies with humans.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: I'll leave you to it then.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Do you need to prepare lots of gifts?

dialogues.speaker: Yolotli
dialogues.text: No no, actually the opposite, really...

dialogues.speaker: Yolotli
dialogues.text: Above all else, Iktomisaurs despise it when other creatures try to use their abilities for selfish gain. They won't be so easily bribed.

dialogues.speaker: Yolotli
dialogues.text: Before inviting them, you must follow their etiquette and state the purpose for which you require their help.

dialogues.speaker: Yolotli
dialogues.text: But they're sharp-eyed as all get-out, so there's no point trying to fool them.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: What if it's a gift given without expecting anything in return?

dialogues.speaker: Yolotli
dialogues.text: Well... that depends on how much the Iktomisaurus trusts you.

dialogues.speaker: Yolotli
dialogues.text: After all, there's no such thing as a free lunch. The less is asked in returned for a gift, the more suspicious it is.

dialogues.speaker: Yolotli
dialogues.text: Want to give it a try? Well, I've heard the Iktomisaurs love these mushrooms, so good luck.
